A record-only entry has no edit operands, so the checkable surface is its factual claims plus one question the earlier entries in this wave did not raise: whether the artifact being recorded is still a current measurement. I resolved that by comparing the recorded artifact's own pins against live, and by comparing the head-to-adoption gap of this entry against the three record entries that precede it.

findings.title: The entry records exact-bytes-leftover-join.v4 as a current G07 leftover remasurement, but v4 was measured at HEAD 5d5d778 and asserts required-now 26 against a live 28; v4's own remeasurement clause has fired because file 08 has moved twice since, and the entry neither discloses the gap nor records a re-measured successor
findings.where: Title, Decision item 1, and the 'Live remeasurement at draft time' paragraph

measured.recordedArtifactPins: Frozen v4 carries head 5d5d778, file08Pin 3a9442d1 and requiredNowUnchanged 26. Live is HEAD 3b48d8c, file 08 f909ddff and required-now 28. All three of v4's governing values are superseded.
measured.v4sOwnClauseHasFired: v4's remeasurementClause reads 'If a cited file moves in a way that is not append-only COORD growth or COORD heading hygiene, with file 08 … unmoved, re-measure before recording.' File 08 is a cited file and it moved twice — D-167 and D-169 both wrote gate rows. The precondition v4 set for its own recording is triggered.
measured.precedentInThisSeries: Every prior record entry recorded an artifact whose head was the immediately-preceding adopted commit and whose requiredNowUnchanged equalled the live value at recording time. D-170 recorded doctor-actor v11 at head 892236a with 28 when live was 28. D-171 recorded permission v9 at head 81e706b with 28 when live was 28. D-164 recorded doctor-actor v2 at head 665415a with 26 when 26 was live. D-172 proposes recording v4 at head 5d5d778 with 26 when live is 28 — the only entry in the series whose head-to-adoption gap spans a change to a value the recorded artifact asserts.
measured.theEstablishedRemedy: Twice within this same wave the corpus met exactly this condition and answered it by issuing a re-measured successor and recording that: doctor-actor v9 carried a stale 26 and was rejected, v10 and v11 followed, and D-170 recorded v11. Permission v7 was rejected after D-169/D-170, v8 and v9 followed, and D-171 recorded v9. No exact-bytes v5 exists; the chain stops at v4.
measured.notDisclosed: The draft contains zero occurrences of 5d5d778, of 3a9442d1, of 'stale', of 'historical' and of 'as of'. Its only 26-like tokens are inside the date 2026. A reader of the adopted entry would not learn that the artifact it records was measured at a superseded head under a superseded cardinality.
measured.theRemeasurementSentenceIsScoped: The entry does say 'Codex remasured on the live post-D-171 tree and found D-167 through D-171 do not change this subject's obligation routing.' I verified that independently and it holds — the routing is G07-specific and none of D-168 through D-171 touches G07 or DR-103 substantively. But routing is not the only thing v4 asserts, and requiredNowUnchanged is precisely the assertion those acts did change. The sentence is true and does not reach the defect.

findings.whyMustFixNotShouldFix: It is not a wording imprecision that a reviewer can wave through with a note. Recording v4 as written would put an artifact asserting required-now 26 into the permanent record two acts after it became 28, sitting alongside D-170 and D-171 which recorded artifacts asserting 28 — a record that contradicts itself on a condition-4 fact depending on which entry a reader resolves. The same condition at artifact level was a blocker one wave ago, when doctor-actor v9 asserted 26 against a live 28 and was rejected rather than recorded. And the fix is a substantive act, not an edit to this draft's prose: either issue a re-measured v5 and record that, as the two precedents this entry's own masthead invokes both did, or restate the entry so it records v4 explicitly as a measurement as of HEAD 5d5d778 with the superseded cardinality disclosed. Both are changes a coordinator must choose between; neither is available to me.
findings.whatIsNotWrong: Everything else in the entry checks out, including every claim it makes in its own voice. Its live remeasurement figures are correct against the live register, all eight cited digests recompute, and the routing claim it rests on is independently true. v4's substantive G07 content is also unaffected — its liveGateOwners entry for DR-G07 still equals the live owner cell, and its file08StatusToken still equals the live DR-G07 token. This finding is about which artifact is being recorded and how, not about whether v4's G07 measurement was right.
findings.fix: Either issue exact-bytes-leftover-join.v5 re-measured against HEAD 3b48d8c, file 08 f909ddff and required-now 28, obtain dual ACCEPT, and record v5 — the path D-170 and D-171 both took — or amend this entry to record v4 explicitly as a historical measurement as of HEAD 5d5d778, stating that its requiredNowUnchanged of 26 is superseded by the live 28 and that the recording asserts nothing about current cardinality.

observationsNotFindings: Everything the entry says in its own voice is accurate. Its live figures are current, its digests all recompute, its class claim is true, and its routing claim survives independent testing. The defect is not in what it asserts but in what it proposes to record — which is why it took comparing the recorded artifact's pins against live, rather than reading the entry more carefully, to find it.

The 'Wave 2' label recurs from D-171, again with zero occurrences in live COORD. I declined it there and decline it here for the same reason, but two entries in a row now carry a term the record does not define. If wave labelling is meant to be traceable it wants a definition in COORD; if it is scratch process framing it wants removing before adoption.

The head-to-adoption gap is a cheap and general test, and I had not been running it. D-170 and D-171 both recorded artifacts written at the immediately-preceding adopted commit; this one reaches back three. A gap is not itself a defect — artifacts are always frozen before the entry that records them — but a gap that spans a change to a value the artifact asserts is exactly what the artifact's own remeasurement clause exists to catch. I have added it to the checks I run on record-only entries.

It is worth being precise about what is not in question: v4's G07 measurement itself still holds against the live register. Its liveGateOwners entry for DR-G07 equals the live owner cell, its file08StatusToken equals the live DR-G07 token, and none of D-167 through D-171 disturbs its obligation routing. A re-measured v5 would very likely carry the same ten obligations with the same flags — the difference would be three governing pins and one cardinality.

decision.scopeOfObject: OBJECT on one MUST-FIX. Every dispatch prohibition holds and every claim the entry makes in its own voice is true. The objection is to what it records: exact-bytes-leftover-join.v4, measured at HEAD 5d5d778 with required-now 26, being recorded as a current G07 leftover remasurement against a live HEAD 3b48d8c and required-now 28, with v4's own remeasurement clause fired by two intervening file-08 writes and neither the gap disclosed nor a re-measured successor issued.
decision.summaryForCoordinator: One MUST-FIX. Everything D-172 says in its own voice is accurate — all eight cited digests recompute, its live figures match the register exactly at 28 of 28, 32 of 32, DR-G32 last and DR-G07 OPEN, its class claim against D-170 and D-171 is true, and its routing claim survives independent testing, since none of D-168 through D-171 touches G07 or DR-103 and D-167's single DR-103 mention is not substantive. What I object to is the artifact it records. Frozen v4 carries head 5d5d778, file08Pin 3a9442d1 and requiredNowUnchanged 26; live is 3b48d8c, f909ddff and 28. v4's own remeasurement clause says re-measure before recording if a cited file moves, and file 08 moved twice under D-167 and D-169. The entry's remeasurement sentence is scoped to obligation routing and is silent on the cardinality those acts did change, and the draft contains zero occurrences of 5d5d778, 3a9442d1, 'stale', 'historical' or 'as of', so a reader of the adopted entry would not learn of the gap. The precedent is what makes this stand out rather than a quibble: D-170 recorded doctor-actor v11 at head 892236a with 28 when live was 28, D-171 recorded permission v9 at head 81e706b with 28 when live was 28, and D-164 recorded v2 with 26 when 26 was live. D-172 would be the only entry whose head-to-adoption gap spans a change to a value the recorded artifact asserts — and the corpus met exactly this condition twice in this wave and answered it by issuing a re-measured successor, which is why no exact-bytes v5 existing is the salient fact. I graded MUST-FIX because the remedy is a substantive act rather than a rewording: issue and record a v5 measured at the live head, or restate the entry to record v4 explicitly as a historical measurement with the superseded cardinality disclosed. v4's G07 content itself is not in question — its DR-G07 owner and status token still match live. I also verified my own Stage A verdict completely and it is genuinely ACCEPT 0/0; I did not read the Codex Stage A verdict or the Codex counterpart for this subject, which appeared mid-review. 'Wave 2' recurs from D-171 with no referent in COORD, flagged not charged.
